trust_decision.summary: Strip ANSI/VT100 escape sequences from attacker-supplied CSP-report fields before they are written to the terminal; decided in the csp_report handler by sanitizing document-uri, blocked-uri and violated-directive at extraction, then printing the sanitized copies.

landing_point.why: The only handler for the unauthenticated POST /__csp__ route; this is where the advisory's report fields are read straight out of request.get_json and later printed at line 211.

fix_sites.entry_point: POST /__csp__ reaches it indirectly (helper _sanitize_terminal defined in the same module)
fix_sites.module_kind: server module helper (Flask static-file serving module)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The unsupported-directive branch only turns an unknown report into a 500 and never reaches the report-printing block, so it looks like error handling rather than the logging path the advisory is about; likewise the asset routes look like a different feature.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The same print() deliberately emits Mesop's own ANSI colour codes (tc.RED/GREEN/CYAN/YELLOW/MAGENTA/RESET) and non-ASCII box-drawing/emoji characters; a fix that strips escape sequences or control/non-ASCII characters from the whole formatted message, or replaces it with repr(), destroys that intended console formatting, and the generated keyword_arg snippet must still contain the plain origin.

O6_input_shapes: string field with CSI sequence (ESC [ ... final byte)
OSC sequence terminated by ESC backslash
non-string field value coerced with str() (e.g. integer)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: POST /__csp__ with an unsupported violated-directive (e.g. img-src) still raises Exception("Unexpected CSP violation:", violated_directive, report) carrying the raw, unsanitized report dict (document-uri/blocked-uri) into the traceback Flask logs to the terminal.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It is just the error branch for a directive Mesop does not support; it 500s instead of printing the report, so it looks unrelated to the reporting output.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same function, 10 lines below the sanitized reads

O8_uncovered_routes.route: GET /__web_components__/<path with no '.'> raises MesopException("Unexpected request to " + path) with the raw percent-decoded URL path; uncaught, so Flask logs the traceback containing the escape bytes to the terminal.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Different endpoint (web-components asset route) with nothing to do with CSP reporting; it is a rejected request, not a log message.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, ~40 lines above the landing point; 0 packages

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second raise that embeds the same request path/extension in an exception message, on the serving_path branch
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: A maintainer hardening the web-components route would add the same _sanitize_terminal call next to each of the two existing 'Unexpected request' raises; the code already duplicates the message.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: sanitizing attacker-influenced WebSocket parse errors before logging.error("Failed to parse message: %s", ...)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This is the other place attacker bytes reach a log call, so a maintainer following the advisory's own reasoning would extend the helper there.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: routing untrusted messages through warn(), which already prefixes ANSI codes and logs the raw message
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It is the project's existing warning channel; a maintainer might consolidate the CSP report warning there and would then need sanitization in the wrapper.

O9_family: log/terminal output injection: improper neutralization of ANSI escape sequences and CR/LF in logged attacker-controlled data (CWE-150 escape-sequence injection, CWE-117 log forging)

O10_build.toolchain: Bazel py_test (mesop/server/BUILD static_file_serving_test) plus plain pytest via the root conftest.py stubs; deps flask, werkzeug, absl-py, protobuf, python-dotenv, msgpack, pydantic, deepdiff
O10_build.project_tests: mesop/server/static_file_serving_test.py (bazel target static_file_serving_test, mesop/server/BUILD:77-81) covers only gzip/send_file_compressed; mesop/tests/e2e/web_security_test.ts only snapshots CSP headers; nothing at the pinned commit exercises POST /__csp__

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Strip only ESC[..m-style colour codes (or strip escapes from the fully formatted message) around the print, leaving the raw report dict that the exception branch still emits.
